text:
alex.k: Hey — following up on the rollout RFC. I want to sketch a small refactor: split the decision plane (policy evaluator) from the routing plane, and define a compact rollout policy DSL. Thoughts?
priya.s: +1 on separation. we hit scaling issues when policy logic blocks routing threads.
jordan: can you clarify the failure modes we want the fallback to handle? retries, model OOMs, degraded quality?
samuel: all of the above. Also transient infra blips (region/network). fallback should be able to route to cheaper or older model variants automatically.
alex.k: exactly — three classes: correctness regressions (quality), infra (latency/errors), and cost spikes. each needs different signals and cooldowns.
priya.s: for correctness we need human-reviewed canaries + eval sets. for infra use p50/p95/p99 latency + error budget burn. cost spikes we can have a conservative throttling policy.
jordan: interface boundary idea: policy svc returns a short JSON decision {action, target_variant, ttl, reason_code}. router applies decision. keeps decisions cached until ttl.
samuel: love that. simple contract. want to see the JSON shape.
alex.k: quick draft shape: 
```
{"action":"divert|hold|continue|rollback","target":"model:v1|v0-quant","ttl_s":60,"score":0.87,"reason":"latency:99>500ms"}
```
priya.s: prefer reason codes over free text for automation. also add a signal_version/hash so we know decision derivation.
jordan: how do we avoid split-brain across regions? decisions need to be region-aware and optionally global. store in a fast kv with region preference.
samuel: agree. region-local decisions default, global override for org-wide incidents. TTLs must be conservative to prevent flapping.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: New rollout policy pushed to staging by @alex.k at 5270001240 :eyes:
priya.s: TL;DR on rollout schedule — we should support weight ramps, sample-based canaries, and a fast-escape path (single API toggle) for SREs.
ajordan: question on data-plane fallback: do we let router do per-request hedging or centralize at edge? per-request hedging increases load.
alex.k: tradeoff: hedging lowers tail latency but can double cost. propose configurable hedging per route with budget. example: hedging only for <100ms tail budget.
samuel: what about model-variant fusion? if variant A fails quality checks but is cheaper, maybe route 90% to stable and 10% to A for low-risk queries. need a risk-tier label on requests.
priya.s: yep. add "risk_tier": "interactive|background|batch" in policy. console should surface this.
jordan: telemetry: we need per-route signal fidelity + causal logs. keep decision traces (policy inputs) for postmortem. long-term: move policy simulator into CI so every change runs dry-runs.
alex.k: action items: 1) priya to write minimal DSL doc + reason codes, 2) jordan to prototype decision response schema and kv caching, 3) sam to draft SRE rapid-escape API and default throttles.
priya.s: I'll add a small example DSL later today.
jordan: I'll spin up a PoC that returns decisions and measure latency under load.
samuel: will draft escape API, will include an emergency rollback toggle + audit trail.
alex.k: cool — aim to sync next Tue. also note: keep API surface tiny so Dedicated/Private can implement locally without whole platform.
priya.s: one more thought: signals TTLs should be versioned and explicit. stale signals must not trigger rollback.
jordan: agree — add `signal_version` and `signal_observed_ts` in inputs.
ops-bot: reminder: retro thread created for rollout playbook updates.
alex.k: thanks everyone. short thread but good alignment.
